source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client on haloperidol develops torticollis and oculogyric crisis. What is given?
questions.rationale: Acute dystonia is treated with IM benztropine or IM/IV diphenhydramine.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Acute Dystonia (PDF p. 245)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Shuffling gait, mask-like face, and pill-rolling tremor on antipsychotics indicate:
questions.rationale: Pseudoparkinsonism mimics Parkinson's; treated with anticholinergics or amantadine.
questions.quote: Coarse pill-rolling movements of the thumbs and fingers while at rest.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client on antipsychotics cannot sit still and paces anxiously. This is:
questions.rationale: Akathisia is inability to sit still with restlessness; beta-blockers or benzodiazepines may help.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which statement about tardive dyskinesia is correct?
options: It appears in the first day
It is cured by more drug
questions.rationale: TD is often permanent, appears after months of therapy, and involves oral-facial movements.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tardive Dyskinesia (PDF p. 246)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client on antipsychotics has high fever, rigidity, and unstable BP. What is FIRST?
questions.rationale: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome requires immediate discontinuation and treatment of hyperthermia and dehydration.
questions.quote: Immediate discontinuance of all antipsychotic medications

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which lab is monitored weekly on clozapine?
questions.rationale: Clozapine can cause agranulocytosis; WBC is checked at baseline and weekly.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client forgets an antipsychotic dose and remembers 6 hours late. What should he do?
questions.rationale: If more than about 4 hours late or near the next dose, omit the forgotten dose.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Antipsychotic Responsibilities (PDF p. 247)
questions.quote: If the missed dose is more than 4 hours late or the next dose is due

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Why are TCA prescriptions given in small amounts to depressed clients?
questions.rationale: TCAs are potentially lethal in overdose, so limited amounts reduce suicide risk.
questions.quote: Potentially lethal if taken in an overdose.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which antidepressant class is also effective for OCD?
questions.rationale: SSRIs are effective for OCD and have fewer side effects than TCAs.
questions.quote: Effective in the treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which drug is dangerous to combine with an MAOI?
questions.rationale: MAOIs are not given with other MAOIs, TCAs, meperidine, or CNS depressants.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which cheese is allowed on an MAOI diet?
questions.rationale: Avoid aged cheeses; cottage, cream, ricotta, and processed cheese slices are allowed.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which antidepressant has a higher risk of seizures?
questions.rationale: Bupropion causes seizures at about 4 times the rate of other antidepressants.
questions.quote: Can cause seizures at rate 4 times that of other antidepressants

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which antidepressant can cause priapism?
questions.rationale: Trazodone can cause priapism.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Other Antidepressants (PDF p. 248)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: What is the THERAPEUTIC lithium level?
questions.rationale: Therapeutic lithium is 0.6–1.2 mEq/L; above 3.0 may require dialysis.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Why should a client on lithium avoid heavy sweating?
questions.rationale: Fluid and sodium loss from sweating increases lithium levels rapidly.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Mood Stabilizers (PDF p. 250)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which mood stabilizer can cause Stevens-Johnson syndrome?
questions.rationale: Lamotrigine: SJS; valproic acid: hepatic failure; carbamazepine: aplastic anemia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Mood Stabilizers (PDF p. 250)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which mood stabilizer can cause hepatic failure?
questions.rationale: Valproic acid can cause fatal hepatic failure.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Mood Stabilizers (PDF p. 249)
questions.quote: Valproic acid can cause hepatic failurein fatality

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Why is alcohol dangerous with benzodiazepines?
options: One drink may act like three
questions.rationale: Benzodiazepines strongly potentiate alcohol.
questions.quote: One drink may have the effect of three drinks

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Why must benzodiazepines not be stopped abruptly?
questions.rationale: Benzodiazepine withdrawal can be fatal; stop only under supervision.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A child on methylphenidate for ADHD should be monitored for:
questions.rationale: Stimulants cause anorexia, weight loss, irritability, and insomnia.
